title: Tool Execution & Sandbox Primitives
summary: This module provides core primitives for executing tools across different environments (e.g., Python in a JS sandbox) and for managing data serialization and representation within interactive REPL contexts for language models.

nodes.label: Generate Python Tool Wrapper
nodes.title: Python Tool Wrapper Generator
nodes.description: Dynamically creates Python function code that acts as a wrapper for external tools. This generated code facilitates calling JavaScript-bridged tools from a Python sandbox, handling argument serialization and result deserialization.

nodes.label: Execute Tools via JS Bridge
nodes.title: JavaScript Tool Call Bridge
nodes.description: An asynchronous JavaScript function that serves as a bridge for executing tools. It sends JSON-RPC requests to a host environment and processes the responses, enabling cross-environment tool invocation from a Python sandbox.

nodes.label: Define Sandbox Object Serialization
nodes.title: Sandbox Object Serialization Interface
nodes.description: An abstract base class for objects that need to be serialized and deserialized for use within a sandboxed execution environment. It defines methods for setup, byte serialization, sandbox reconstruction, and LLM-friendly previews.

nodes.label: Represent REPL Variable Metadata
nodes.title: REPL Variable Metadata Model
nodes.description: A Pydantic model that encapsulates metadata about a variable available in a Read-Eval-Print Loop (REPL) environment. It can generate itself from a value and format its details for inclusion in prompts for language models.

nodes.label: Python Sandbox Environment
nodes.title: Python Execution Sandbox
nodes.description: Represents a sandboxed Python execution environment, such as Pyodide, where generated tool wrappers run and interact with the JavaScript bridge for external tool calls. It's where Python code is executed securely.

nodes.label: External Tool Host
nodes.title: External Tool Execution Host
nodes.description: The environment outside the Python sandbox where the actual tool functions are defined and executed. It receives tool call requests from the JavaScript bridge and returns their results.

nodes.label: Language Model
nodes.title: Language Model for Interaction
nodes.description: Represents a large language model that interacts with the REPL environment. It consumes formatted variable metadata to understand the state and available data, guiding its decision-making and code generation.

groups.label: Tool Bridging & Execution
groups.title: Cross-Environment Tool Execution
groups.description: This group manages the process of defining, invoking, and executing tools across different runtime environments, specifically bridging Python sandbox execution with external host environments via a JavaScript intermediary.

groups.label: Sandbox Data Management
groups.title: Data Serialization and REPL Representation
groups.description: This group focuses on how complex data types are prepared for and represented within a sandboxed execution environment and how their metadata is formatted for consumption by language models in a REPL context.
